newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's defense minister declares emergency rule.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's defense minister declares emergency rule.

text.p: Ecuador's defense minister declared a nationwide state of emergency on Friday in an attempt to help quell protests against President Abdala Bucaram, who was ousted by Congress on Thursday but defiantly refused to step down.
Defense Minister Victor Bayas imposed the state of emergency with immediate effect as fresh protests against Bucaram erupted in Quito and the Pacific coast city of Guayaquil.

Police fired tear gas into a crowd of about 5,000 demonstrators in central Quito to prevent them from marching on Independence Square, just outside the ornate Carondelt presidential palace, where Bucaram has been holed up since his dramatic ouster.
There were no immediate reports of injuries in the clash between demonstrators and police in Quito. But local media reports said at least two people were hurt in anti-Bucaram protests in Guayaquil.

"I believe it is necessary to declare a state of national emergency to preserve the country's peace," Bayas, a retired army general, said on national television. He did not specify what individual guarantees would be suspended under emergency rule.
